analysis:
All changes are documentation only. docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md: date bump and a new head paragraph (lines 13-15) saying Nemotron Super VL has no qualified RAM tier and its native builder is unregistered/internal. No security controls change. docs/reference/README.md line 10 only adds a link to nemotron-super-image-formats.md; the target page is not in the supplied evidence. docs/reference/configuration.md adds four env-var rows at head lines 320-323: DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP (opt-in, default off), _MTP_DEPTH (1-3), _MTP_VERIFICATION (rectangular/serial), and _MAX_CONCURRENT (1-64, default 1). The rows are documented as not forwarded to LaunchAgents, and invalid values fail the load. I saw only a truncated patch excerpt of these rows, not the Swift sources (NemotronSuperLocalMTP.swift, NemotronSuperLocalAdmission.swift).

Relevant threat IDs: T-041/TB-007 (prefix cache). The docs say the speculating owner refuses media, but I cannot verify prefix-cache or SSD behavior for the Super owner. Concurrent batched decode with MAX_CONCURRENT>1 could touch cross-request isolation (A-001, T-028). That is a code-level question outside the supplied evidence and not a documentation regression. No new endpoints, auth, attestation, or threat-model assumption changes. Later passes should check whether the underlying Swift change (not supplied) affects KV/prefix-cache scoping, memory admission, or the env-var trust boundary with the local operator (TB-003, which already assumes operator control of the environment).
